exposure: Serum cholylglycine (CG) level in pregnant women
outcome: Neonatal Apgar scores (at birth, 1 min, 5 min)
cohort: The study included 40 pregnant women with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) and 40 normal pregnant women, selected from 663 pregnant women admitted to Daqing Longnan Hospital.
finding: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) was associated with lighter birth weight, earlier gestational week at birth, lower neonatal Apgar scores, and higher levels of inflammatory cytokines, with maternal serum cholylglycine (CG) levels positively correlated with adverse fetal outcomes and markers of inflammation/hepatic dysfunction.
cross-section timing: July 2016 to December 2017, with measurements taken around the time of birth.
birth_weight: Measured, found to be lighter in the ICP group.
gest_age: Measured, found to be earlier in the ICP group.
